newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to push N.Korea on stranded Japanese spouses.
newsitem.headline: Japan to push N.Korea on stranded Japanese spouses.

text.p: Japan will press North Korea to allow all of an estimated 1,800 Japanese women who moved to North Korea with their Korean husbands in the 1960s and 1970s to visit their homeland, the top government spokesman said on Wednesday.

Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama refused to comment on media reports Tokyo and Pyongyang would hold talks on the women in the Chinese capital of Beijing this week, but said that all women who wanted to should be allowed to visit Japan.

"The government strongly hopes that North Korea will respond to these problems," Kajiyama told reporters, listing the Japanese wives issue among Tokyo's other grievances with its Stalinist neighbour and former colony.

Tokyo has cited the issue of the wives, suspicions that Pyongyang agents have abducted at least 10 Japanese and customs agents' recent seizure of a North Korean ship laden with illegal narcotics as reasons why it has not responded to appeals for food aid to famine-struck North Korea.
The issues have also kept Japan from establishing diplomatic ties with the northern half of Korea, which it ruled from 1910-45. Tokyo and Seoul normalised ties in 1965.
The government estimates that some 1,800 Japanese women left for North Korea with their Korean husbands between 1959 and 1982.

Most of the Japanese women, whose Korean husbands are descendants of Koreans who moved or were brought to Japan before World War Two, have not been heard from for years, and North Korea has not allowed the women to visit their families in Japan.
Widespread reports of looming famine in the isolated and impoverished country have given urgency to the relatives' long campaign to learn of the women's fate.
